Bound request superset for patching a product attribute.

Flat, not a discriminated union like create: ``type`` is not patchable, so there is no
discriminator in the PATCH body (nor in a reconstructed sub-path fragment) to resolve a
union at bind time. This DTO therefore accepts the union of every type's patchable field.

Per-type narrowing happens server-side: ``AttributeService.patch`` fetches the attribute's
concrete type and re-validates the set fields against the matching per-type subtype DTO
(see ``ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_TO_UPDATE_DTO``), rejecting fields that don't apply to that type.

``label``, ``group_ids`` and ``product_family_ids`` are intentionally not patchable:
v1's patch path doesn't handle ``label``/``groups``, and product-family attribute
membership is an async, destructive operation that must stay a separate job.

Input DTO for patching a product family.

``name`` is the only patchable field. Attribute membership (``attributes``,
``parent_attributes``, ``variant_attributes``) is intentionally absent: in PIM those are
link/unlink/edit-level operations that return a Job, because the family write is followed
by an unbounded propagation across the family's products that also *deletes* attribute
values off variants whose parent now owns them. v1's own family PATCH reflects this by
hard-coding ``columns = ["name"]``, so an attribute field in the body would be silently
dropped; ``extra="forbid"`` rejects it instead.

v1 loads the family PATCH body without ``partial=True`` and its ``name`` is
``required=True``, so a patch that sets no field at all is rejected: the hook's own
empty-payload guard catches that before the PIM round-trip.

upstream.description:
Input DTO for patching a product.

The linkable list relations (categories, static lists, channels, ecatalogs, product data
sheets) are not fields here: each is linked one id at a time with
``POST /products/{id}/{relation}`` and unlinked with ``DELETE /products/{id}/{relation}/{id}``.
Assets are managed through media attributes.

``gtin`` is non-nullable while its neighbour ``label`` is: PIM's ``ProductUpdateSchema``
declares ``gtin = fields.Str()`` with no ``allow_none``, so a forwarded ``null`` comes
back as ``{"gtin": ["Field may not be null."]}``. Rejecting it here turns that into a
field-level error at the kernel boundary instead of a PIM round-trip.
Parent product ID (for variants); null detaches the product from its current parent
Product family ID; null unassigns the product's current family
Input DTO for creating a relationship.

Input DTO for patching a relationship.

``name`` is the only patchable field: ``label`` is derived and dump_only in v1's
``RelationshipSchema`` (and non-writable in ``RelationshipManager.writable_columns``),
and ``status`` is managed by the delete flow, not by callers.

Standard response envelope for every non-DELETE operation.

Exactly one of ``data`` / ``errors`` is populated:

* GET / CREATE / BULK_CREATE / BULK_DELETE / BULK_PATCH / UPDATE success → ``data`` is the returned object/value.
* SEARCH success → ``data`` is a list of results.
* Failure → ``errors`` is set, ``data`` is an empty list.

Example::

    # GET / CREATE / BULK_CREATE / BULK_DELETE / BULK_PATCH / UPDATE success
    OperationResponse(data={"id": 1, "name": "Widget"})

    # SEARCH success
    OperationResponse(data=[{"id": 1, "name": "Widget"}])

An error-shaped instance (``errors`` set) is what a registered exception
handler returns — see :mod:`plytix_api_tools.core.exception_registry`.
Application code signals failure by raising, not by constructing one of
these directly.
